title: Prompt fingerprint proxy cache and KV residency orchestration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: We observe duplicated KV entries for common prompt prefixes across concurrent requests and tenants. This leads to wasted GPU slab residency and extra memory pressure during continuous batching, increasing latency tail and reducing effective throughput. Existing dedupe approaches are either too slow (content-addressable slabs at request time) or too aggressive (global eviction causing cache thrash).
solution_overview: Introduce a lightweight host-resident "proxy fingerprint cache" that maps canonical prompt fingerprints to a compact residency token and placement hints. The proxy acts as a fast first-check during request enqueue/continuous-batch assembly: if a fingerprint is present and marked GPU-resident, the batching layer references the residency token instead of re-inserting an identical KV fragment. For near-duplicates we emit a delta-prefetch hint so the GPU can materialize only missing attention keys. Complement with a per-GPU KV residency orchestrator that tracks 'slot credits' and enforces microstriping to avoid large contiguous slab ownership by a single tenant. The orchestrator coordinates background compaction and async eviction during low-util periods.
detailed_design: - Fingerprinting: canonicalize prompt templates and variable slots; compute a 64-bit stable fingerprint (SipHash) at request ingress. Store a small metadata entry in host memory with: fingerprint, model-variant, sequence-length-bucket, and residency token.
acceptance_criteria:
- 20% reduction in GPU KV resident bytes for the benchmarked multi-tenant chat workload (p95 throughput case).
- No increase in median token latency beyond 5%.
- Continuous batching path uses residency token for >= 60% of cacheable prefixes in steady state.
- No correctness regressions (identical outputs for canonicalized prompts).
implementation_plan: 1) Proxy cache data structure in host: compact hash table with TTL and sequence-bucket eviction. 2) Residency token API: small integer referencing per-gpu-slot + version. 3) Integrate check into request enqueue: on fingerprint hit and token valid -> mark request as 'KV-ref' (skips insert). 4) Adjust continuous-batching assembler to group 'KV-ref' requests and attach residency tokens to batch header. 5) GPU runtime: map residency token to GPU slab pointer when forming microbatches; if token stale trigger async fetch. 6) Orchestrator: periodically compute slot-credit scores and initiate compaction tasks. 7) Feature flag gated rollout and metrics.
testing_and_metrics:
- Unit tests for fingerprint collisions and canonicalization rules.
- Integration test with synthetic interleaved tenant workload reproducing prior duplication.
- Performance bench: baseline vs proxy cache on p95 throughput, measure GPU resident bytes, average tokens/sec, median/p95 latency.
- Metrics to emit: proxy_hit_rate, residency_token_staleness_rate, async_fetchs_per_1k_requests, gpu_kv_reserved_bytes, slot_credit_balance_per_gpu.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag and limited to one region. 2) Canary on small set of dedicated machines during low-traffic windows. 3) Monitor metrics for 48h, check for increased async fetchs or tail latency. 4) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% for dedicated pools. 5) For Hosted API, enable for customers on runtime-1.22 opt-in only.
risks_and_mitigations:
- Collision risk: use conservative canonicalization and a stable 64-bit hash; run a collision detector job in staging.
- Stale residency token causing extra async fetches: mitigate with short TTL and immediate invalidation on compaction event.
- Multi-tenant fairness: microstriping and slot credits to prevent monopolization by large tenants.
- Complexity in GPU mapping: keep residency token mapping logic minimal and well-tested; provide a fallback full-insert path if mapping fails.
notes: This approach aims to shift cheap checks to host-side fast paths and reduce redundant GPU inserts during continuous batching. It is intended to complement, not replace, existing content-addressable slab techniques; long-term we can merge indexing strategies once stable. Consider collaboration with storage team for a shared fingerprint ledger to survive process restarts.
comments: 2026-02-16 - Design sync: reviewed with infra and runtime leads. Consensus to prototype host proxy first and avoid GPU-visible metadata schema changes.

2026-02-22 - Prototype results: host proxy reduced duplicate insert attempts by ~38% in microbench with 1K concurrent short-session chats. Observed 9% improvement in token throughput, GPU resident bytes dropped by ~14%.
2026-03-03 - Review feedback from security: acceptable (no PII stored in fingerprint). Add note to canonicalization doc to strip timestamps/user-ids.

2026-03-08 - QA: integration test found race where token invalidation and batch assembly overlap causing a rare mapping failure. Adding a short lock and fallback to full insert fixed the repro in staging.

2026-03-10 - Performance update: after locking fix, p95 latency unchanged, p99 improved by 6% for our mixed-tenancy benchmark. Next: instrument staleness_rate and run 7-day dogfood to observe long-tail behavior.
